prospects.thesis: SMCI is a direct beneficiary of the ongoing AI data center buildout, providing high-density GPU server platforms tightly integrated with NVIDIA's Blackwell and next-gen accelerator roadmap. At a 0.6x P/S with bullish options flow and institutional accumulation, the risk/reward is compelling as hyperscaler capex remains elevated into 2027. Recent liquid-cooled rack deployments and improving governance overhang position the name for multiple re-rating.

Booz Allen is the leading pure-play federal AI/cyber services firm, with roughly two-thirds of revenue tied to defense and intelligence agencies actively scaling AI mission workloads. At 0.8x P/S with bullish options positioning and institutional support, BAH offers defensive cash flow with an AI-services growth kicker as FY27 DoD software and autonomy budgets expand. Book-to-bill trends and Thundercat/AI contract wins are the near-term catalysts.

UiPath is pivoting from pure RPA into agentic AI automation with its Autopilot and Agent Builder platforms, addressing enterprise demand for GenAI workflow orchestration. At 5.0x P/S with bullish options flow and institutional accumulation, the setup is improving but execution risk remains after prior guidance resets. A confirmed ARR reacceleration would validate the agentic thesis.

Kratos is a pure-play on unmanned systems, tactical drones (Valkyrie/CCA), and hypersonic targets — the fastest-growing line items in the DoD budget under the Replicator initiative. Bullish options and institutional flow reflect rising conviction that CCA production awards and Golden Dome-related propulsion contracts drive step-function revenue growth into 2027. Premium 7.8x P/S is justified by category leadership in autonomous airpower.

AeroVironment is the dominant Western small-UAS supplier (Switchblade, Puma, JUMP 20) with strong replenishment tailwinds from Ukraine, Taiwan, and DoD loitering munition programs following the BlueHalo acquisition integration. Institutional accumulation supports the view that FY27 loitering munition backlog and directed-energy exposure justify the 4.7x P/S multiple. Provides differentiated small-cap drone exposure versus KTOS's jet/CCA focus.

market_pulse.rotation_analysis: Big money is piling into the classic defensive and rate-sensitive playbook right now — Real Estate, Healthcare, Utilities, and Energy are all seeing unusually heavy bullish call buying, which tells me traders are positioning for the Fed to start cutting rates and are also betting Washington's next moves will favor these groups (think drug pricing deals getting finalized, energy permitting reform, and infrastructure/data-center power demand keeping utilities bid). On the flip side, they're quietly bailing on or hedging Technology and Materials in a big way — Materials in particular has an absurd 47x volume spike on puts, which screams tariff retaliation fears and a China demand scare, while Tech looks like people finally locking in gains ahead of potential AI antitrust action, export controls, or just plain "this thing ran too far" profit-taking. The bearish bets on Comm Services and Staples plus widening credit spreads (HYG and LQD both loaded with puts) tell me the smart money thinks the consumer is weakening and corporate borrowing is about to get more expensive — that's usually a signal for a choppy, defensive market over the next 4-8 weeks where boring beats exciting. The interesting contradiction: stocks broadly are near highs but the options tape looks like people preparing for a growth scare, so either the hedgers are wrong or the index is masking real damage happening underneath. The non-obvious tell nobody's talking about: that Materials print is so extreme it's either one whale making a specific tariff/trade-war bet, or someone with a very good read on an upcoming executive order — when you see a 58 put/call ratio, somebody knows something, and it's worth watching headlines on China, steel, and critical minerals over the next two weeks.
